note: The unspent half of the construct-2jb.4 corpus. Authored 2026-08-04 by eight independent agents, one per setting, each of which was instructed to read no file in this repository — not the catalog, not the matcher, not the other corpora — and wrote its eighteen situations from the setting alone. That is the authorship discipline construct-gsf named and the earlier corpora lacked: the corpus and the thing it measures do not share an author. Labels were then assigned twice, by two independent coders who likewise saw only the ten domain names and their one-line concerns, never the keyword lists. The two coders agreed exactly on 127 of 144 outcomes; the other 17 were adjudicated afterwards and each outcome records both raw label sets so the adjudication can be argued with; across all 144 outcomes of both halves that is exact agreement 127/144, Krippendorff alpha (MASI) 0.8955, recorded here once because nothing in the repo may read the sealed half to recompute it. CAVEAT THAT TRAVELS WITH EVERY NUMBER TAKEN FROM THIS FILE: authors, coders and adjudicator are all models of one family, so observed agreement is an upper bound on independent agreement (correlated error, construct-2jb.3's caveat, unchanged here).
partition: SEALED. Nothing in src/ or scripts/ may read this file, and tests/kernel/implication/corpus-split.test.ts enforces that. It exists so that one honest generalization measurement remains available after unspent-outcomes.json has been measured against and is therefore spent. Breaking the seal is a decision with a date and a reason, not a convenience: score it once, record the number, and mark this file spent in the same commit.
discipline: Identical to unspent-outcomes.json; the two halves are one authoring pass split deterministically by position inside each setting, so both carry all eight settings and neither is one author's whole output.
